answer: In an agent market serving lotus growers, the bidding inlet admits each identity only after it locks 100 coins in escrow for 30 days; the same coins cannot back another identity during that period. An attacker creating 1,000 bidders must therefore immobilize 100,000 coins, pushing available liquidity toward its nadir. The bonds are refundable, but borrowing costs and foregone returns make mass fake identities expensive.
